newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 18.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
PRESIDENT'S RULE IN UTTAR PRADESH

Uttar Pradesh has again been put under President's rule and its newly constituted state assembly under suspended animation. The federal government took this step following the inability of any party to form a popular government in the state. The polls held recently in the state had resulted in a hung assembly. Article 356 of the constitution was invoked by the President who proclaimed central rule in Uttar Pradesh after the cabinet decided in its favour.
The Economic Times
SIXTY-ONE FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT PROPOSALS OKAYED

The Industry Ministry has okayed 61 proposals with foreign direct investment worth over 7.75 billion rupees and exports of 15.5 billion rupees. U.S. based Bechtel Corp has been allowed to set up a wholly owned subsidiary ($8 million) to establish a design, engineering and procurement subsidiary to provide export services. Foster Wheeler Corp's proposal for a wholly owned subsidiary (175 million rupees) for designing and supplying steam generating and related auxiliary equipment has been cleared. Other major wholly owned subsidiaries cleared include those of Britco Foods (4.4 billion rupees) and Sandoz.
EIGHT PCT CAP FOR 30 TO 90 DAY DEPOSIT SCHEMES LIKELY

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) may introduce a new slab of deposit rate for deposits under one year in the forthcoming credit policy. In a bid a pull down short-term deposit rates, RBI may create a separate slab of 30 to 90 days and cap the interest rate at eight percent. At present, deposit rates under one year are capped at 11 percent and those over a year are free. This slab is likely to continue with the cap at 10 percent, bankers said.
Financial Express
TEXTILE POLICY REINTRODUCES NON QUOTA SHARE

The government reintroduced non-quota exporters' entitlement and earmarked a separate category for new investors in the newly announced textile policy for 1997-99. The policy stressed exports and called for stricter monitoring of export quotas. Under the new policy for garments, the number of systems was increased to four from two. Past performance entitlement was fixed at 75 percent which included five percent for high value entitlement. The new investors entitlement and first come first served entitlement was pegged at 10 percent each.
Business Standard
ULTIMATUM TO BASIC TELECOM OPERATORS TO SIGN PACTS

Communications Minister Beni Prasad Verma issued an ultimatum to six basic telecommunication companies to sign the licence and interconnect pacts by Friday or face legal consequences under the tender conditions. The minister's warning came as a shock to the companies holding letters of intent for providing basic telecommunication services in six circles. Meanwhile, the Department of Telecommunications said the basic services licence would be made assignable.
RUPEE LESS LIKELY TO SLIDE AGAINST DOLLAR

Foreign market circles feel the rupee will not come under any downward pressure in the coming months, despite the repayment hump. They also feel the central bank may effect a percentage point cut in export refinance rates and packing credit to boost exports. The central bank, according to dealers, may allow banks to lend funds out of their foreign currency non-resident (FCNR) deposits in the local market. This would reduce the downward pressure on the rupee and make the greenback easily available in the market, they said.
BOURSE REGULATOR TO CHECK CARTELISED PRICE HAMMERING

The bourse regulator (SEBI) is learnt to be exploring ways to check cartelised hammering by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) of scrips of Indian companies on the eve of their global depository receipt (GDR) offerings. The Finance Ministry and the capital market watchdog have agreed to formulate a policy to check this menace. SEBI has been asked to examine the issue. Recently, the Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd named certain FIIs who had hammered its scrips after on the eve of the company's GDR offerings.
MERRILL LYNCH PEGS GDP GROWTH AT 6.5 PCT

Merrill Lynch's latest report on the Indian economy has forecast a gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 6.5 percent for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). It said the country's export outlook was good since the economies of Japan and Europe were likely to recover soon. Japan and Europe account for 34 percent of India's exports. Faster export growth should contribute to GDP growth, Merrill added. It predicted high capital inflow, which should facilitate higher rate of investment than permitted by domestic savings. Inflation was likely to come down to the 6-7 percent range as a result of tightening of the monetary policy by the central bank, said Merril.
IBRD PRESSURISES INDIA TO OPEN UP INSURANCE

The World Bank and International Finance Corporation (IFC) are putting pressure on India to open up its insurance sector. The issue is likely to figure in talks between the visiting World Bank team led by its president J.D. Wolfensohn and government officials. The World Bank and IFC have been insisting that their clients draft comprehensive insurance policies should cover project risks. The World Bank has asked the state-owned insurance companies that did not offer coverage for risks to rework their policies. The National Thermal Power Corporation, the biggest borrower from World Bank, has taken measures to strengthen its risk assessment capabilities.
NODAL AGENCIES TO MONITOR USE OF WORLD BANK FUNDS

The government will set up an elaborate co-ordination mechanism to monitor utilisation of World Bank funds in the country. This will apply to the states and federal ministries that absorb large amounts of World Bank funds. In a meeting between the visiting World Bank president and the Finance Minister, it was decided to explore ways to enlarge the Bank's presence in the education, health and infrastructure sectors. The IBRD chief said the Bank would enhance its assistance programme if the quality of loan utilisation was improved.
Financial Express
INDO-UK TRADE RECORDS 14 PCT GROWTH

India and Britain are exploring ways to expand bilateral trade. The Indo-British Partnership (IBP), a bilateral trade body, is identifying new areas to develop trade and investments. IBP co-chairman Sir Terence Harrison said Indo-British trade had gone up by 14 percent in the first seven months of fiscal 1996-97 (April-March). Indo-UK trade grew 70 percent in the last three years. In the apparel and metal manufacture sectors the increase in Indian exports to Britain was 1.2 and 5.8 percent, respectively. Britain's exports to India in the power generating machinery, iron and steel and paper sectors increased by 43, 71 and 90 percent respectively.
FAKE BLUE CHIP SCRIPS BOOMING ON BOURSES

The fake shares menace, once the bane of trading on the Bombay bourse (BSE), has begun to dog the National Stock Exchange (NSE). Counterfeiters are understood to have recently pushed through fake shares worth 10 million rupees through a leading company with a high turnover. These include blue chips like State Bank of India, ITC Ltd, Bajaj Auto, Reliance, ICICI, Hoechst, Ranbaxy Labs and the UTI Mastershare.
The Observer
RAILWAYS PROPOSE 650 BLN RUPEE INVESTMENT

The railways have proposed an investment of 650 billion rupees during the Ninth Plan period (1997-2002), as against 331.24 billion rupees during the Eighth Plan. The massive investment is aimed at helping the railways meet the growing demand for freight carrying capacity. The railways hope to carry a freight traffic of 523 million tonnes by the end of the Ninth Plan.
HOUSING CORP (HFDC) DROPS GLOBAL (GDR) OFFERING

The Housing Development Finance Corporation (HFDC) has deferred its $150 million global depository receipt issue. HFDC has decided to focus on raising funds from the fixed deposit market. The company has raised over six billion rupees in the last six months through its fixed deposits programme. Now, it is reportedly targetting eight to nine billion rupees of net additions to its fixed deposits in the next six months.
Business Line
INDIA TO BE EXPORT BASE FOR ADTRANZ LOCOS

Adtranz (ABB Daimler Benz Transportation) plans to use India as its export base for worldwide sales of high powered electric locomotives and components after 2000 AD. Adtranz has already set up a manufacturing facility for electrical and electronic components for AC drives at Baroda and signalling equipment at Halol. It is carrying on negotiations for a bid floated by the Railways for developing a Traffic Management System in Mumbai. Adtranz has also formed a consortium with Itochu of Japan and other firms to bid for the Delhi Mass Rapid Transport System.
